features.text: The patient is a 45-year-old male.
The patient has right elbow pain.
The elbow pain has been present for about three weeks.
The elbow pain is sharp and shooting, like it's stabbing.
The elbow pain is exacerbated by using the elbow, such as reaching for something in the cupboard.
The patient does not have swelling or redness.
The patient has difficulty moving the elbow without pain.
The patient has no previous injuries or surgeries on the right elbow.
The patient has no history of repetitive strain in the upper extremities other than recent tennis.
The patient has not undergone any physical examination or imaging studies for the elbow pain.
The pain is triggered by gripping objects, lifting things, and extending the arm.
The pain is located on the outer (lateral) side of the right elbow.
The pain is near the lateral epicondyle.
The patient has no numbness, tingling, or weakness in the hand or fingers.
The patient has no swelling, redness, or warmth around the elbow.
The patient has not experienced locking, clicking, or popping sensations during elbow movement.
The patient has no prior imaging or physical examination of the right elbow.
The pain is triggered during tennis play, especially when hitting the ball and following through with the arm.
The patient has no previous episodes of elbow pain or injury related to tennis or other activities.
The patient is willing to undergo a physical examination and imaging studies such as an X-ray or MRI.
